name: Sadiqabad–Gadra Road Highway
history: National Highway 70 runs through the western desert of Rajasthan towards Gadra Road, a small settlement in Barmer district close to the international border. It is a thinly trafficked road across open sand country, and its main users are the villages strung along it and the security forces who patrol the frontier.
facts: Runs through the far western desert of Barmer district.
Gadra Road, at its end, sits close to the India–Pakistan border.
One of the emptiest national highways in the country — long stretches have no settlement at all.
It serves border villages that have very few other road links.
significance: Roads in the border desert exist as much for security and for the isolated villages along them as for through traffic. This is one of those roads.
travelNotes: Remote. Fuel, water and mobile coverage are all unreliable. Some areas near the border need permits, so check locally before travelling.

sources.title: NHAI — National Highways Authority of India
